records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — --flusher-processes accepts negative integers, creating an empty process map that causes shard assignment to raise KeyError and prevents consumer startup; require a positive integer.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a behavioral inconsistency. In the diff at line 51: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. When `max_processes` is None (not provided), this defaults to the number of assigned shards. However, the CLI option at line 434 sets `default=1`. This means: (1) CLI consumers get 1 flusher process by default, (2) Programmatic callers that don't pass `flusher_processes` get one process per shard.
